newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Brokers say Handelsbanken to bid for Stadshypotek.
newsitem.headline: Brokers say Handelsbanken to bid for Stadshypotek.

text.p: Swedish brokers said they expect banking group Handelsbanken to announce a bid for mortgage institute Stadshypotek at a news conference due to be held at 1500 GMT on Thursday.

"Handelsbanken's press conference announcement should not only mean that it will place a bid on Stadshypotek, but also that (insurer) Skandia did not want to, or could not, match that bid," a broker told Reuters.
"A press conference should also mean that Handelsbanken is confident it has a bid that will be attractive for all shareholders," he said.

Handelsbanken's bid could, for example, consist of a cash offer for the state's 34 percent stake in Stadshypotek and a choice between cash and Handelsbanken shares for other shareholders, the dealer said.

Several analysts told Reuters that Handelsbanken's announcement and the suspension of shares in both the bank and the mortgage insititute could only be interpreted as Handelsbanken intending to launch a bid.
Handelsbanken is the only Swedish bank that could afford to pay for Stadshypotek in cash, analysts say.
The boards of Skandia and Stadshypotek proposed a merger between the two last month before the government last Monday received bids for its stake.

The proposal did not go down well with Finance Minister Erik Asbrink who insisted on seeing through the planned controlled auction of the government's stake and said he did not have any confidence in Stadshypotek's board.
